paper_metadata.title: Quantum algorithms for hedging and the learning of Ising models

experiments.description: Theoretical passive quantum Hedge algorithm for estimating the total accumulated loss over T rounds using amplitude estimation and oracular access to loss vectors.

algorithm.variant: Quantum estimation of the total loss of the Hedge algorithm

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Loss oracles U_{l(t)} provide access to each loss vector entry l_j^(t) in superposition; weights are computed from prior loss oracles and used to estimate p^(t)·l^(t).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate total Hedge loss L_H = sum_{t=1}^T p^(t)·l^(t) to relative accuracy epsilon.

problem_instance.description: Online learning / hedging over T rounds with N strategies and adversarial losses.

dataset_specification.description: Oracular online loss vectors l^(t) in [0,1]^N; no concrete dataset specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: None reported beyond oracle access and rescaling of weights by w_max.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical guarantee only; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct weight vectors from prior losses and rescale by w_max.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Sum per-round estimated losses to obtain total loss estimate.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in N; quadratic-like improvement from N to sqrt(N)
speedup_claims.conditions: oracular access to loss vectors; passive setting; T may be much smaller than N
speedup_claims.caveats: Runtime worsens in T; no empirical benchmark; output is a classical estimate of total loss.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T^2 sqrt(N) / epsilon) queries; eO(T^2 sqrt(N) / epsilon) gates

experiments.description: Theoretical active quantum Hedge algorithm that samples a strategy from the portfolio state and incurs transaction cost C0 per round.

algorithm.variant: Active Hedge algorithm with transaction cost and quantum sampling

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare quantum state |p^(t)⟩ proportional to sqrt(p_j^(t)) and measure to sample a strategy j(t).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Sample a strategy each round so that expected loss remains close to Hedge loss while reducing transaction cost.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Sampling-based portfolio allocation; one strategy selected per round.

problem_instance.description: Online hedging with transaction costs over T rounds and N strategies.

dataset_specification.description: Oracular loss vectors l^(t) in [0,1]^N; no concrete market dataset specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Minimum-finding used to compute w_max; state preparation via amplitude amplification.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical regret and bias analysis only; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Find minimum cumulative loss to rescale weights; prepare approximate probability state.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure sampled state and query loss oracle for selected strategy.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical Hedge algorithm with sampled flag

speedup_claims.conditions: oracular access; active betting with quantum sampling; transaction cost per strategy C0
speedup_claims.caveats: Worsens in T; regret bound holds with high probability; sampling introduces bias controlled by xi.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T^2 sqrt(N) log(T/delta)) queries; eO(T^2 sqrt(N) log(1/delta)) gates

experiments.description: Classical approximate Sparsitron that estimates inner products instead of computing them exactly, used as a hybrid/classical baseline improvement over the original Sparsitron.

hyperparameters.lambda: known l1 norm bound on w
hyperparameters.T: number of training samples for main loop
hyperparameters.M: number of samples for empirical risk estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability vector p^(t) is stored in a sampling data structure; inner products p^(t)·a^(m) are estimated from samples.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn GLM parameter v such that risk epsilon(v)=E[(sigma(v·X)-sigma(w·X))^2] is at most epsilon.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond l1-norm bound ||w||_1 <= lambda.

problem_instance.description: Generalized linear model learning from two training sets: one of size T for online updates and one of size M for empirical risk selection.

dataset_specification.description: Samples (x^(t), y^(t)) in [-1,1]^N x [0,1] and (a^(m), b^(m)) in [-1,1]^N x [0,1]; no named dataset specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Inner products estimated to additive accuracy epsilon/(16 lambda) for risk estimation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical guarantee only; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Build sampling data structure for p^(t); estimate inner products for empirical risk.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select t' minimizing approximate empirical risk and output v=lambda p^(t').

speedup_claims.factor: improvement over original Sparsitron in some parameter regimes; no quantum speedup
speedup_claims.conditions: when N > 1/epsilon^2, approximate inner products reduce runtime
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a classical/hybrid improvement only; sample complexity remains near-optimal and unchanged.

experiments.description: Quantum Sparsitron for learning generalized linear models using quantum inner-product estimation and amplitude amplification/estimation.

hyperparameters.lambda: known l1 norm bound on w
hyperparameters.xi: accuracy for preparing |q>, used in state preparation
hyperparameters.h(t): inner product estimate at step t
hyperparameters.z(t,m): inner product estimates for empirical risk

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum access to training examples x^(t) and a^(m) via oracles U_train1^(t) and U_train2^(m); loss circuits compute 1/2(1+(sigma(lambda h)-y)x_j).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn GLM parameter w such that epsilon(v)=E[(sigma(v·X)-sigma(w·X))^2] <= epsilon.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: l1-norm bound ||w||_1 <= lambda; multiplicative weights update with estimated losses.

problem_instance.description: Generalized linear model learning from two training sets, with quantum access to features and labels.

dataset_specification.description: Training samples (x^(t), y^(t)) in [-1,1]^N x [0,1] and (a^(m), b^(m)) in [-1,1]^N x [0,1]; no named dataset specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Estimate p^(t)·x^(t) to additive accuracy epsilon/(8 lambda^2) and p^(t)·a^(m) to additive accuracy epsilon/(16 lambda).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical proof of learning guarantee and runtime; no empirical evaluation reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct loss oracles from training data; estimate inner products and empirical risks; compute q_j classically from stored estimates.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select t' minimizing estimated empirical risk; optionally prepare quantum state |q> and use it for classification of new samples.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in N; sqrt(N) dependence instead of linear N
speedup_claims.conditions: quantum access to training data; amplitude amplification/estimation; oracular model
speedup_claims.caveats: Runtime worsens in T and epsilon; sample complexity unchanged; output is classical estimates plus optional quantum state preparation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: eO(lambda^2 T^2 M sqrt(N) / epsilon log(1/delta))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: eO(N lambda^2 / epsilon^2 log(1/delta) + lambda^6 / epsilon^6 log^3(1/delta)) for approximate Sparsitron; original Sparsitron eO(N lambda^2 / epsilon^4 log^2(1/delta))

experiments.description: Corollary applying the Quantum Sparsitron to learn Ising models from samples, yielding quantum speedup in the dimension N.

algorithm.variant: Quantum learning of Ising models via Quantum Sparsitron

hyperparameters.T: number of independent samples from the Ising distribution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum query access to entries of samples from the Ising distribution; learn matrix A* via repeated Quantum Sparsitron runs.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn Ising interaction matrix A* such that ||A - A*||_max <= epsilon.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Width bound lambda on the Ising model; reduction from GLM learning.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: P[Z=z] ∝ exp(sum_{i,j:i≠j} A_ij z_i z_j + sum_i theta_i z_i)

problem_instance.description: N-variable Ising model with width at most lambda.

dataset_specification.description: Samples from an Ising distribution; no concrete graph or dataset name specified.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Apply Quantum Sparsitron O(N) times, once per node, to reconstruct rows/columns of A*.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical guarantee only; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Run Quantum Sparsitron separately for each node/row/column of the Ising model.

speedup_claims.conditions: learning Ising models via repeated Quantum Sparsitron runs; quantum query access to samples
speedup_claims.caveats: Improves N dependence but worsens in T and epsilon; no empirical validation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: eO(lambda^2 T^2 M N^(3/2) / epsilon log(1/delta))
